title: Farnsworth Art Museum receives four murals by artist N.C. Wyeth from the Bank of America Art Collection
summary: The Farnsworth Art Museum announced the acquisition of four monumental murals by celebrated American artist Newell Convers (N.C.) Wyeth (1882–1945), a gift of Bank of America. Commissioned more than a century ago by the First National Bank of Boston, a predecessor institution of Bank of America, the mural cycle depicts, through the artist’s perspective, scenes of maritime trade and commerce in New England. “This is an extraordinary gift to the Farnsworth and an important addition to our collection of work by the Wyeth family,” said Christopher J. Brownawell, Executive Director of the Farnsworth Art Museum. “These murals demonstrate N.C. Wyeth’s remarkable abilities as a painter and storyteller on a grand scale, while their subject matter speaks directly to New England’s maritime heritage. We are deeply grateful to Bank of America

title: Milestone sets house record with $1.8M toy auction that drew hot international competition
summary: Twelve years after opening their gallery doors in metro Cleveland, Milestone Auctions recorded its highest-grossing auction ever, a $1.8 million sale of premium-quality antique and vintage toys. The October 17 event featured rarities that seldom, if ever, appear in the marketplace, including an elusive Machine Man Robot that landed at the top of prices realized with a selling price of $134,550. Manufactured by Masudaya (Japan) in 1960, Machine Man represents the rarest of a quintet of large, boxy tin robots that collectively became known in the toy hobby as the “Gang of Five.” The example auctioned by Milestone was one of only a handful of its type known to exist in such high condition. “Even the most advanced robot collection would not be considered complete without a Machine Man, so on the rare occasion that one becomes available to purchase—especially one as nice as the one we offered—it’s

title: Roland presents property from Park Avenue estate at November 14th auction
summary: Roland Auctions NY will feature an important collection of fine jewelry, antique furniture, Art and Decorative items, mostly from a very prominent New York City Park Avenue estate, at their upcoming fall auction on Saturday, November 14th, 2026 at 10am. title: Sotheby's to offer extraordinary 1962 letter from Brian Jones recruiting Charlie Watts to The Rolling Stones
summary: More than six decades after it was written, an extraordinary handwritten letter from Brian Jones to Charlie Watts, in which Jones attempts to recruit the drummer to join the fledgling group that would soon become The Rolling Stones, will be revealed to the public for the first time. Written in June 1962, before the group had even adopted The Rolling Stones name and just weeks before their first performance that July, the letter comes directly from Watts’s sister, having remained in the family for more than sixty years. Accompanied by its original envelope, the letter will make its auction debut at Sotheby’s New York’s Rock & Pop sale on 15 December, with an estimate of $70,000 - 80,000. Addressed to “Mr. C. title: Naked ambition: The book that cemented Newton's global reputation, in a landmark international new edition
summary: Some things age gracefully. Others refuse to behave. Fifty years on, Helmut Newton’s first publication, a book that elevated his name far beyond the pages of fashion magazines, returns in a landmark, international re-edition. First published under the titles White Women and Femmes secrètes in 1976, it brought together fashion, portraiture, and the erotic in a visual language that was cool, controlled, and unapologetically provocative. Here are the women: glamorous, commanding, seductive, and in control. Here are the clothes, cars, hotels, pools, bedrooms, and immaculate interiors. Here are the cultural icons of the time, from Paloma Picasso, Veruschka and Elsa Peretti to Karl Lagerfeld, David Hockney, and Charlotte Rampling. And here’s Newton, orchestrating it all with his famously sharp eye and subversive sense of humor. title: Brooklin A. Soumahoro explores geometric abstraction in new exhibition at Mennour
summary: Onto what worlds do Brooklin A. Soumahoro’s Windows open? From the outset, the geometric abstractions brought together in this exhibition invite the gaze to an experience both optical and chromatic. Each canvas develops from a complex arrangement of repeated and combined triangular motifs, following a system of its own. The triangle is the elementary unit, the module from which the entire composition is built. This organisation is the result of extensive preparatory work. In pencil, Soumahoro constructs geometric structures, adjusting their proportions through precise mathematical calculations before exploring the many ways they can be combined. Yet this rigorous discipline gives rise to a state of instability that the artist calls “perfect unbalance”. title: Danish painting attributed to Wilhelm Marstrand for nearly a century identified as work by Adam Müller
summary: A painting that has been attributed to Danish artist Wilhelm Marstrand for nearly a century has been identified as the work of Adam Müller (1811–1844), a gifted but short-lived pupil of C.W. Eckersberg. The discovery, announced by Nivaagaards Malerisamling, is among the findings of new research that challenges established attributions and sheds light on the often-forgotten individuals who posed for artists during Denmark's 19th-century Golden Age. The painting, Liggende model (Reclining Model), was created in 1833 and is considered one of the most celebrated Danish studies of a live model. Depicting a reclining female nude viewed from behind, the work is distinguished by an unusually sensual treatment of the human body, contrasting with the more restrained academic conventions of its time. Art historian Jesper Svenningsen established the new attribution while researching his forthcoming book, En plads på podiet

title: Shota Nakamura debuts quiet, desaturated landscape paintings at Mendes Wood DM Brussels
summary: Mendes Wood DM is presenting seven lakes, Shota Nakamura’s first solo presentation with the gallery and his first solo exhibition in Belgium. The show returns to the desaturated, dreamlike terrain of Nakamura, an artist who works as readily from memory as from observation. The Brussels space, with its fireplaces and separate rooms that distinguish it from a white cube, set Nakamura thinking about scale, and he has approached much of the exhibition through medium and small formats as an antimonumentalist choice. The choice plays on a dialectic built into a foundational premise of landscape painting: outdoor observation is returned to us, in miniature, to be viewed indoors. “With a small painting, you have to physically come closer to it,” he says. “Because of the scale, a very small mark or a slight shift in color can become surprisingly significant.” Throughout, Nakamura returns often to lakes and to clouds. title: Jane Benson reimagines Mary Shelley's 'Frankenstein' in new solo exhibition 'her her'
summary: her her debuts a major new series of monumental, mixed-media works by New York-based conceptual artist Jane Benson. Benson’s acclaimed practice spans drawing, sound, new media, and sculpture, often appropriating and unraveling existing literature and found objects. her her features a new series of text-based drawings that reframe Mary Shelley’s Frankenstein as a lyrical exploration of womanhood and rage. Particularly urgent in the current moment, Benson’s work fragments and distorts legibility while amplifying Shelley’s singular voice. The works in her her are grounded in the chapters of Frankenstein narrated by the monster himself. Benson reads his narrative of self-creation and isolation as a parallel to Shelley’s own, situating the text within a larger feminist discourse. title: Sotheby's sells rare Nanotyrannus specimen 'Jodi' for $47.3 million
summary: "Jodi," the extraordinarily rare Nanotyrannus specimen, sold at Sotheby's for $47.3 million, after a twelve-minute bidding battle that saw six bidders compete online and over the phones, before ultimately selling on the phone. With today's result, "Jodi" becomes the second most valuable dinosaur ever sold at auction, surpassed only by "Gus," which achieved $50.1 million at Sotheby's this July. "This auction would not have been possible without the hard work and dedication of Clayton Phipps (the Dinosaur Cowboy) and Pete Larson, as well as the wonderful team of people who worked together with Clayton to excavate and save "Jodi": Jodi Pierson, Kelly Pierson, Luke Phipps, Nathan Cooper, Katie Busch, and Chris Morrow. Their passion and expertise have been fundamental to Jodi's story. title: AGWA to unleash candy-coloured landscapes and a world of wonder this Summer
summary: This December internationally celebrated WA artist Pip & Pop transforms AGWA into a dazzling parallel universe of colour, sugar and wonder. AGWA presents Double Magic, an immersive exhibition by renowned Perth artist Tanya Schulz, working as Pip & Pop. Bursting with playful imagination, the exhibition invites visitors into a fantastical dream world where curiosity is rewarded and the unexpected awaits at every turn. Part enchanted forest, part candy kingdom and part psychedelic daydream, the exhibition invites visitors of all ages to step away from reality and enter a mini universe where creatures, sparkling landscapes and impossible abundance collide. At the centre of this extraordinary world is a fantastical cat shaped cave. Visitors might look inside, marvel at its magical splendour and bask amongst a landscape bursting with colour, hidden details and fantastical forms. title: Laura Carralero reinterprets 14th-century medieval frescoes in new Galleria Continua exhibition
summary: GALLERIA CONTINUA is presenting Tempo Manifesto, the first solo exhibition in Italy by Cuban artist Laura Carralero, whose painterly practice explores the relationship between architecture, memory and the perception of space. Conceived specifically for GALLERIA CONTINUA's San Gimignano space, the exhibition brings together a group of previously unseen oil paintings on panel created between 2025 and 2026. The works emerge from the artist's engagement with the town's medieval heritage, particularly the frescoes by Memmo di Filippuccio in the Camera del Podestà of the Palazzo Comunale, alongside references to Bernardo Daddi and Ambrogio Lorenzetti. Carralero isolates architectural elements, canopies, textiles and ornamental motifs from these fourteenth-century images, removing them from their original narrative context and transforming them into autonomous forms that invite reflection on time and the construction of space. title: Helen Frankenthaler's Hint from Bassano to be united for the first time with the masterpiece that inspired it
summary: In the summer of 2027, two connected paintings created four centuries apart will meet for the first time at the National Gallery. Monumental works made by Italian Renaissance artist Jacopo Bassano (1510–1592) and the American Abstract painter Helen Frankenthaler (1928–2011) will be united in the exhibition Frankenthaler and Bassano. Frankenthaler’s five-metre-wide Hint from Bassano (1973) will be displayed next to the painting that directly inspired it, Bassano’s The Flight into Egypt (about 1544–45) – an exceptional loan from the Norton Simon Museum, Pasadena (California). Throughout her career, Frankenthaler selected works by artists she admired as starting points for her own. title: Taipei Fine Arts Museum hosts major Ryuichi Sakamoto retrospective
summary: Taipei Fine Arts Museum presents Ryuichi Sakamoto / seeing sound, hearing time, the first large-scale exhibition in Taipei devoted to the late composer, music producer, and artist Ryuichi Sakamoto (1952–2023). The exhibition looks back on Sakamoto’s groundbreaking artistic practice from the 2000s onward. It features seven large-scale installations, as well as selected archival materials from his 1999 opera LIFE, highlighting his long-term collaborations with five artists and art collectives: Shiro Takatani, Daito Manabe, Carsten Nicolai, Apichatpong Weerasethakul, and Zakkubalan. By tracing back Sakamoto’s reflections on time, life, the environment, and technology, the exhibition reveals how he developed new forms of expression and sensory experiences of sound, opening up different ways for us to listen to and feel the world. title: Marie Jose Gallery opens Matthew Corbin Bishop solo exhibition
summary: ‘One of the first things I ever bought was a globe. I was seven. My childhood was spent surrounded by symbols of nations: atlases, books of flags and maps of the world, which I would sketch. I learned every world capital, every flag, and collected as many currencies as possible. The work in this exhibition stems from that love of nations. It is a project that has been a focus for over 15 years: The Making of the Modern World, the postage stamp as the central element of reimagining the world through visual currency. Throughout this time, I read extensively to develop an understanding of Europe and the Ottoman (Turkish) Empire’s colonial history, and as the project advanced, my research informed new ideologies and ways of working. title: Ippodo Gallery presents modern interpretations of Japanese kana script in 'Leaves of Words'
summary: Ippodo Gallery is presenting Leaves of Words, on view October 30 to December 5, 2026. Three masters delve into modern interpretations of Japanese script in three unique materials: calligraphy written by Satoshi Nemoto, forged iron sculpted by Tsuneo Nakazawa, and raden lacquer inlaid with mother-of-pearl by Shinya Yamamura. "Japanese poetry takes the human heart as its seed and grows into myriad leaves of words." Preface to the Kokin Wakashū, the earliest kana anthology written by the author Ki no Tsurayuki c. 905. Kana emerged in the ninth century, when Japanese writers began abbreviating Chinese characters into a phonetic script of their own. In the Heian court, it flourished as the language of poetry and love letters—supple, cursive, and written in a single continuous breath; as much drawing as writing. summary: Sotheby's opened its new, expanded gallery and salon in Dubai to the public, marking the company's tenth year with a physical presence in the UAE and the start of a significant new era for the business. title: Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo presents Andrea Bowers solo exhibition
summary: Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo presents a solo exhibition by Andrea Bowers, Los Angeles-based artist who, for more than three decades, has developed her practice at the intersection of activism and the visual arts. In her work, the artist employs different media, from drawing and painting to installation and video, to explore issues of social justice and advocacy and to celebrate overlooked figures and events from the history of social struggles. Her exhibitions are developed through a methodology based on the artist’s close engagement with communities and social movements, through community life and discussion, participation in demonstrations, the building of activists’ networks, and archival research. title: Armenian Museum of America strengthens leadership team with appointment of Sarah Hayes as Deputy Director
summary: The Armenian Museum of America (AMoA) is pleased to announce the appointment of Sarah Hayes as Deputy Director, expanding her leadership role at the Museum and positioning her to support the institution’s continued growth, strategic development, and national visibility. Hayes has served as Director of Development since 2023, leading membership, grant management, donor relations, corporate and foundation partnerships, and events. In her new role, she will retain leadership of the Museum’s development program while taking on broader responsibilities across the institution. summary: The John and Mable Ringling Museum of Art Foundation, Inc., announced newly elected executive officers and appointments of four new members to its Board of Directors for the 2026–2029 term. title: Dulwich Picture Gallery announces first UK museum exhibition by Charlie Mackesy
summary: This winter, Dulwich Picture Gallery will welcome the truly original and magical drawings of award-winning author and illustrator Charlie Mackesy. Bringing together never-before-seen early sketches, unpublished studies, and original works from across Mackesy’s career, the one-room exhibition will offer audiences of all ages a unique insight into his creative process, celebrating the universal message that art is for everyone. Charlie Mackesy: The Boy, the Fox, the Mole, the Horse... And You will run from 3 November 2026 – 7 February 2027, specially curated by art historian, curator and author Kate Bryan. Visitors will encounter rarely displayed preparatory sketches alongside finished illustrations from Mackesy’s internationally best-selling books The Boy, the Mole, the Fox and the Horse and Always Remember: The Boy, the Mole, the Fox, the Horse

title: Fortes D'Aloia & Gabriel presents Barrão's solo exhibition 'Troca de segredos' in São Paulo
summary: Fortes D’Aloia & Gabriel presents Troca de segredos [Exchange of secrets], an exhibition of new sculptures and watercolors by Barrão at FDAG Jardins, in São Paulo. The works are assembled from porcelain fragments drawn from an inventory of ornaments and utilitarian objects collected from secondhand markets: conches, giant strawberries, elephants, owls, and other elements from a kitsch universe of household goods. Organized by color and motif in a kind of material library, these objects provide a ready-made palette of finishes and glazes. Working within this formal and chromatic repertoire, Barrão builds abstract structures whose branching contours and proliferating volumes suggest organic growth. title: de Young and Legion of Honor Announce A Dozen Exhibitions to Open in 2027
summary: The Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco announce a full schedule of exhibitions, which will be on view for local audiences and visitors to San Francisco in 2027. Both the de Young and Legion of Honor will be home to major exhibitions that examine cultural and artistic movements born in the Bay Area. Newly announced, original shows on French artists will delight, including Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec at the de Young museum and Simon Vouet at the Legion of Honor. Contemporary artists will be on view throughout the year at both museums, including a fourth rotation of works by local artists mostly drawn from the Svane Family Foundation gift, along with the first major exhibition on the US West Coast dedicated to British-Nigerian artist Yinka Shonibare. title: MTA Arts & Design announces new commissions by Ivan Forde, Trevor Paglen, and Howardena Pindell
summary: MTA Arts & Design announced three major new commissions by acclaimed artists Ivan Forde, Trevor Paglen, and Howardena Pindell. Each will create a permanent, site-specific art installation for a different MTA station. Forde’s large-scale mosaic installation will be featured at New York City Transit’s Broadway Junction ACJLZ ; Paglen will transform a new pedestrian overpass and adjacent parking-garage facade at Metro-North's Southeast station; and Pindell will create a dynamic glasswork for the overpass and stairwell landings at Metro-North's Botanical Garden station.
